lines: Good evening. I’m Hannah Thibedeau, and this is your Palindrome News brief.

Conservative Leader Pierre Poilievre is criticizing a key feature of the Carney government’s latest budget, arguing the proposed $15-million capital gains exemption on the sale of qualifying shares from a Canadian company applies too narrowly, excluding key businesses, CBC News reports.
Goulding had been participating in live-fire exercises at CFB Wainwright last month as part of training for potential deployment overseas, Global News reports.
Hundreds of people gathered at the Royal Canadian Legion in Elmwood to attend a ceremony honouring and remembering Indigenous veterans, CityNews Winnipeg reports.

Nvidia announced Sunday it is launching an independent investigation into its chief executive and founder, Jensen Huang, over concerns he was the “target of a foreign intelligence effort,” The Canadian Press reports.

Pope Leo XIV delivered a diplomatic but subtly strong critique of Argentine President Javier Milei’s austerity measures and libertarian agenda as he arrived Sunday in Argentina, insisting that political leaders must put people, not the economy, first, The Associated Press reports.
Two trains collided Sunday south of the Egyptian capital of Cairo, killing seven people and injuring at least 125, authorities said.
That’s your brief. We’ll keep watching, so you don’t have to.
